intro.title: About OneDocs
intro.paragraph1: OneDocs is an AI-powered intelligent document analysis tool designed to help users quickly extract key information and organize knowledge from PDF documents. Whether it's news highlights, data analysis, or academic notes, OneDocs generates structured analysis results with one click.
intro.paragraph2: Built with the Tauri v2 desktop framework and React 19, OneDocs provides a lightweight, smooth local experience. All document processing happens locally — your data is never uploaded to any third-party server, ensuring privacy and security.
intro.paragraph3: By integrating multiple AI model providers, OneDocs supports flexible model switching to adapt to different scenarios. Four specialized analysis modes — News Overview, Data Analysis, STEM Quick Know, and Liberal Arts Richness — cover a wide range of document types from news to academia.

help.title: Help & Guide
help.content:
# OneDocs Beginner's Guide

Welcome to OneDocs! This tutorial will walk you through installation, configuration, and your first document analysis.

---

## 1. Download & Install

Visit the [OneDocs Releases page](https://github.com/LYOfficial/OneDocs/releases/latest) and download the installer for your OS:

- **Windows**: Download the `.exe` installer (NSIS recommended), double-click to install
- **macOS**: Download the `.dmg` installer, drag to Applications folder
- **Linux**: Download the `.AppImage` or `.deb` package

After installation, launch OneDocs and click "**Start with One Text**" to enter the main interface.

---

## 2. Choose a Model & Configure API Key

OneDocs supports multiple AI model providers. You need to select a model and enter the corresponding API Key to use the analysis features.

### 2.1 Free Models (Recommended for Beginners)

OneDocs includes free models that **require no API Key**:

1. Click "**Settings**" in the top navigation bar
2. Select "**Models**" on the left
3. Choose the **OneDocs** provider (marked as "Free Models")
4. No API Key needed — just select a model

> ⚠️ Free models have limited capacity and may occasionally be unavailable. If you encounter errors, switch to another model.

### 2.2 Paid Models

If you have an API Key from another provider:

| Provider | Recommended Model | Get API Key |
|----------|-------------------|-------------|
| OpenAI | GPT-4o mini | [platform.openai.com](https://platform.openai.com) |
| Zhipu GLM | GLM-4.7 Flash | [open.bigmodel.cn](https://open.bigmodel.cn) |
| DeepSeek | DeepSeek V4 Flash | [platform.deepseek.com](https://platform.deepseek.com) |
| SiliconFlow | GPT-OSS 120B (Free) | [siliconflow.cn](https://cloud.siliconflow.cn) |
| OpenRouter | Various models | [openrouter.ai](https://openrouter.ai) |

**Configuration Steps:**

1. Go to "**Settings**" → "**Models**"
2. Select your provider
3. Enter your **API Key** (required)
4. Enter a custom **Base URL** if needed (optional)
5. Select the model you want to use
6. Click "**Save**"

### 2.3 Local Models (Advanced)

If you have a locally deployed model service, choose **Ollama** or **LM Studio**:

- **Ollama**: Default address `http://localhost:11434/v1`, usually no API Key needed
- **LM Studio**: Default address `http://localhost:1234/v1`, usually no API Key needed

---

## 3. Configure RAG Embedding Model (Optional)

OneDocs uses RAG (Retrieval-Augmented Generation) to improve analysis quality, which requires a SiliconFlow embedding model Token.

### 3.1 Why Do I Need an Embedding Token?

The embedding model vectorizes document content, helping AI understand document structure and semantics more precisely, significantly improving analysis quality.

### 3.2 How to Get One?

1. Register for free at [SiliconFlow](https://cloud.siliconflow.cn/i/AOugEVKt)
2. Free credits are provided upon registration; BAAI/bge-m3 is a free model
3. Get your API Token from the dashboard

### 3.3 Configuration Steps

1. Go to "**Settings**" → "**General**"
2. Find "**RAG Embedding Model Configuration**"
3. Enter your SiliconFlow API Token
4. The status indicator turns green ✅ when configured successfully

> 💡 You can use basic analysis without an embedding Token, but analysis quality may be reduced.

---

## 4. Upload Documents

1. Click "**Analyze**" in the top navigation bar
2. Select an analysis function on the left (see Section 5)
3. Click the "**Click to select documents**" area, or drag and drop PDF files directly
4. **Multiple file upload** is supported — hold Ctrl/Cmd to select multiple files

### File Requirements

- Format: **PDF only**
- Size: Max **30 MB** per file

---

## 5. Choose an Analysis Function

OneDocs offers four specialized analysis modes, selectable from the left sidebar:

| Function | Use Case | Output Structure |
|----------|----------|-----------------|
| **News Overview** | News articles, reports | Core summary + Key information |
| **Data Analysis** | Data reports, statistics | Analysis conclusions + Data details |
| **STEM Quick Know** | STEM courseware, textbooks | Fundamentals + Typical examples |
| **Liberal Arts Richness** | Humanities courseware | Core interpretation + Critical thinking |

---

## 6. File Ordering

After uploading multiple files, you can reorder them by **dragging**:

1. Press and hold a file tag in the file list
2. Drag it to the target position and release
3. File order affects the arrangement of merged results

---

## 7. Start Analysis

1. Confirm you've selected a function and uploaded files
2. Click the "**Start analysis**" button
3. Wait for analysis to complete — the progress bar shows current progress

> 💡 Analysis time depends on document length and model response speed, typically ranging from tens of seconds to a few minutes.

---

## 8. View & Process Results

After analysis completes, results are automatically displayed in the right panel:

### 8.1 Switch View Modes

- **Render mode**: View formatted Markdown rendering (supports LaTeX formulas)
- **Source mode**: View raw Markdown text

### 8.2 Switch Between Files

If you uploaded multiple files, click file tabs to switch between analysis results.

### 8.3 Merge Results

When **2 or more** files have been analyzed, click the "**Merge All**" button to combine all results into one document.

### 8.4 Copy & Export

- **Copy**: Click the "Copy" button to copy Markdown source to clipboard
- **Export**: Click the "Export" button to save results as a `.md` file

---

## 9. Archive Management

Analysis results are automatically saved to the "**Archive**" page:

1. Click "**Archive**" in the top navigation bar
2. The left panel shows a list of historical analysis records
3. Click any record to view detailed results

---

## 10. Other Features

### Appearance Settings

In "**Settings**" → "**Appearance**" you can:

- Switch between **Light/Dark/System** themes
- Adjust **font family** and **font size**
- Set **background color** or upload a **custom background image**

### Language Switching

In "**Settings**" → "**General**" you can switch between Chinese and English interface.

### Format Review

In "**Settings**" → "**General**", enable "**Format Review**" to automatically optimize formatting after analysis, ensuring headings and formulas meet standards.

### Discover Page

The "**Discover**" page shows OneDocs version update history and release notes.

---

## FAQ

### Q: What if I get an error during analysis?

1. Check if your API Key is correct
2. Check your network connection
3. Try switching to another model
4. If using free models, the quota may be exhausted — switch to a paid model

### Q: Formulas display incorrectly in results?

Copy the Markdown source to an external Markdown editor (e.g., Typora, VS Code) for viewing, or export and save as a file.

### Q: What file formats are supported?

Currently only **PDF** format is supported. More formats will be added in the future.

### Q: Is my data safe?

OneDocs is a local application. All document processing happens locally — your files are never uploaded to any third-party server. API calls only send document text content to the model provider.

---

*Current version: v{{version}}*

*For more questions, visit [GitHub Issues](https://github.com/LYOfficial/OneDocs/issues) or [OneDocs Wiki](https://github.com/LYOfficial/OneDocs/wiki)*
